biography: Liam Chen's journey began amidst the bustling streets of Kuala Lumpur, a world away from the roar of engines. His introduction to motorsport was accidental; a chance encounter with a go-kart track on a family holiday. The raw speed and adrenaline ignited a passion that consumed him. From local karting events, Liam rapidly ascended the ranks, showcasing a natural talent that belied his age. A defining moment came at the Malaysian Karting Championship, where, despite starting last due to a mechanical issue, he clawed his way to victory in a breathtaking display of skill and determination. Now, at 17, he's making waves as an independent driver, leveraging sheer talent and relentless self-promotion to carve a path in the fiercely competitive world of motorsports. He's currently seeking sponsorship to compete in Formula 4, his ultimate goal being Formula 1.
drivingStyle: Liam's driving style is best described as aggressive and opportunistic. He thrives on late braking and daring overtaking maneuvers, often pushing the limits of his car and tires. While his raw speed is undeniable, his tire management is still a work in progress. He excels under pressure, often delivering his best performances when the stakes are highest. He has a knack for finding grip where others can't, and his confidence borders on arrogance, which both inspires his team and unnerves his rivals.

rivalries.name: Rajesh Kumar
rivalries.reason: A long-standing rivalry from their karting days, fueled by Kumar's more conservative, calculated approach contrasting with Liam's flamboyant style.

rivalries.name: Isabelle Dubois
rivalries.reason: Dubois publicly criticized Liam's driving as reckless after a near-collision during a regional race, sparking a war of words and fierce on-track battles.

rivalries.name: Kenji Tanaka
rivalries.reason: Tanaka is the son of a racing legend and enjoys factory backing, creating resentment from Liam who feels he's earning his way purely on merit. This difference in their background is the source of constant tension.

quirks: Always wears the same faded lucky t-shirt under his racing suit.
Listens to a specific Malaysian pop song on repeat immediately before every race.
Refuses to walk under ladders, even in the paddock.
famousQuote: "Second place is just the first loser. I race to win, always."
careerHighlight: Winning the Malaysian Karting Championship after starting last, showcasing incredible overtaking skills and racecraft.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of a crucial qualifying session due to overconfidence, costing him a chance to start near the front of the grid and severely impacting his race result.
